evidence.pali: ‘‘Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.
evidence.chinese_simplified: “出息长时，了知：‘我出息长’；入息长时，了知：‘我入息长’。出息短时，了知：‘我出息短’；入息短时，了知：‘我入息短’。学：‘我将觉知全身而出息’；学：‘我将觉知全身而入息’。学：‘我将平静身行而出息’；学：‘我将平静身行而入息’。”
evidence.english: Breathing out long, he knows, 'I am breathing out long'; or breathing in long, he knows, 'I am breathing in long.' Breathing out short, he knows, 'I am breathing out short'; or breathing in short, he knows, 'I am breathing in short.' He trains thus: 'I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body'; he trains thus: 'I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body.' He trains thus: 'I shall breathe out calming the bodily formation'; he trains thus: 'I shall breathe in calming the bodily formation.'

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho cevā tiādīsu arahattaphalasamādhi adhippeto. So hi appitappitakkhaṇe sukhattā paccuppannasukho . Purimo purimo pacchimassa pacchimassa samādhisukhassa paccayattā āyatiṃ sukhavipāko . Santaṃ sukhumaṃ phalacittaṃ paṇītaṃ madhurarūpaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti. Phalasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa hi sabbakāyānugataṃ sukhasamphassaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagataṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppajjati. Imināpi pariyāyena āyatiṃ sukhavipāko. Kilesehi ārakattā ariyo . Kāmāmisavaṭṭāmisalokāmisānaṃ abhāvā nirāmiso . Buddhādīhi mahāpurisehi sevitattā akāpurisasevito . Aṅgasantatāya ārammaṇasantatāya sabbakilesadarathasantatāya ca santo . Atappanīyaṭṭhena paṇīto . Kilesapaṭippassaddhiyā laddhattā kilesapaṭippassaddhibhāvassa vā laddhattā paṭippassaddhiladdho . Paṭippassaddhaṃ paṭippassaddhīti hi idaṃ atthato ekaṃ. Paṭippassaddhakilesena vā arahatā laddhattāpi paṭippassaddhiladdho. Ekodibhāvena adhigatattā ekodibhāvameva vā adhigatattā ekodibhāvādhigato . Appaguṇasāsavasamādhi viya sasaṅkhārena sappayogena cittena paccanīkadhamme niggayha kilese vāretvā anadhigatattā na sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagato . Tañca samādhiṃ samāpajjanto tato vā vuṭṭhahanto sativepullappattattā satova samāpajjati satova vuṭṭhahati. Yathāparicchinnakālavasena vā sato samāpajjati sato vuṭṭhahati. Tasmā yadettha ‘‘ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko’’ti evaṃ paccavekkhamānassa paccattaṃyeva aparappaccayaṃ ñāṇaṃ uppajjati – taṃ ekamaṅgaṃ. Esa nayo sesesupi. Evamimehi pañcahi paccavekkhaṇañāṇehi ayaṃ samādhi pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi nāma vuttoti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于‘此定是现法乐’等语中，意指阿罗汉果定。此定于安止的刹那即是乐，故为现法乐。前前定为后后定乐之缘，故为未来乐果。它能生起寂静、微妙、殊胜、甘美的果心。从果定出定者，缘于遍满全身的乐触与所触，而生起与乐相应的身识。以此理路，它亦是未来乐果。因远离诸烦恼，故为圣。因无欲染、有染、世间染，故为无染。因佛陀等大士所修习，故非凡夫所行。因诸支相续、所缘相续及一切烦恼热恼止息，故为寂静。以不致苦恼之故，而为殊胜。因获得烦恼的止息，或获得止息的状态，故为止息所得。‘已止息’与‘止息’，于义实为一体。或因由烦恼已止息的阿罗汉所获得，故为止息所得。因以专一性证得，或即证得专一性，故为专一性所证得。它不似有漏定，须以有行、有功用之心，降伏对治法、防止诸烦恼而证得，故非以有行降伏防止而得。入此定或出此定时，因已得念圆满，故正念而入，正念而出。或依所预设之时限，正念而入，正念而出。是故，于此，当省察‘此定是现法乐，亦是未来乐果’时，即于自身生起不缘他人的智——此为一分。余分亦同此理。如是，由于此五种省察智，此定被称为具五智之正定。
entries.english: In such phrases as 'this concentration has present happiness and a happy result in the future,' the concentration of the fruit of arahantship is intended. For it is present happiness because it is happiness at every moment of absorption. It has a happy result in the future because each preceding moment is a condition for the happiness of concentration of each succeeding moment. It produces the peaceful, subtle, sublime, and sweet fruition-consciousness. For when one has emerged from the attainment of fruition, body-consciousness accompanied by happiness arises dependent on the tangible object that is the pleasant contact pervading the entire body. In this way too, it has a happy result in the future. It is noble because it is far from the defilements. It is unworldly because of the absence of sensual allurements, the allurements of the round, and worldly allurements. It is not frequented by inferior persons because it is frequented by great persons such as the Buddha. It is peaceful because its factors are pacified, its object is pacified, and all its defilements and anxieties are pacified. It is sublime in the sense of being incapable of causing torment. It is attained through the tranquillization of defilements, or because the state of tranquillization of defilements has been attained. For 'tranquil' and 'tranquillity' are one in meaning. Or, it is 'attained through tranquillization' because it is attained by an arahant whose defilements have been tranquillized. It is attained through one-pointedness because it is attained by means of one-pointedness, or because one-pointedness itself is attained. Because it is not attained by restraining opposing states and warding off defilements with a mind that requires effort and exertion—as is the case with an inferior concentration tainted by taints—it is not a state arrived at by effortful suppression and restraint. One who enters or emerges from that concentration does so mindfully, having reached an abundance of mindfulness; one enters mindfully and emerges mindfully. Or one enters mindfully and emerges mindfully in accordance with a pre-determined period of time. Therefore, when one reviews this concentration thus, 'This concentration has present happiness and a happy result in the future,' knowledge arises in oneself without dependence on another—this is one factor. The same method applies to the rest. Thus, on account of these five kinds of reviewing knowledge, this concentration is called 'right concentration endowed with five knowledges.'

entries.pali: 220 . Sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī ti sabbassa kāyassa paṭi paṭi paccekaṃ sammadeva vedanasīlo jānanasīlo, tassa vā paṭi paṭi sammadeva vedo etassa atthi, taṃ vā paṭi paṭi sammadeva vedamānoti attho. Tattha tattha sabba-ggahaṇena assāsādikāyassa anavasesapariyādāne siddhepi anekakalāpasamudāyabhāvato tassa sabbesampi bhāgānaṃ saṃvedanadassanatthaṃ paṭi-saddaggahaṇaṃ. Tattha sakkaccakārībhāvadassanatthaṃ saṃ-saddaggahaṇanti imamatthaṃ dassento ‘‘sakalassā’’ tiādimāha. Tattha yathā samānepi assāsapassāsesu yogino paṭipattividhāne paccekaṃ sakkaccaṃyeva paṭipajjitabbanti dassetuṃ visuṃ desanā katā, evaṃ tamevatthaṃ dīpetuṃ satipi atthassa samānatāya ‘‘sakalassā’’tiādinā padadvayassa visuṃ visuṃ atthavaṇṇanā katāti veditabbaṃ. Pākaṭaṃ karonto ti vibhūtaṃ karonto, sabbaso vibhāventoti attho. Pākaṭīkaraṇaṃ vibhāvanaṃ tattha asammuyhanaṃ ñāṇeneva nesaṃ pavattanena hotīti dassento ‘‘evaṃ viditaṃ karonto’’ tiādimāha. Tattha tasmā ti yasmā ñāṇasampayuttacitteneva assāsapassāse pavatteti, na vippayuttacittena, tasmā evaṃbhūto sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmi passasissāmīti sikkhatīti vuccati buddhādīhīti yojanā. Cuṇṇavicuṇṇavisaṭe ti anekakalāpatāya cuṇṇavicuṇṇabhāvena visaṭe. Ādi pākaṭo hoti satiyā, ñāṇassa ca vasena tathā pubbābhisaṅkhārassa pavattattā. Tādisena bhavitabba nti catutthapuggalasadisena bhavitabbaṃ, pageva satiṃ, ñāṇañca paccupaṭṭhapetvā tīsupi ṭhānesu ñāṇasampayuttameva cittaṃ pavattetabbanti adhippāyo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 220. “觉知全身者”(Sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī)，即对(入息等)全身的每一部分都如实地有感受、有了知之性；或者，对他而言，对每一部分都有如实的感受；或者，他正对每一部分如实地感受，此为其义。于此，虽以“全”(sabba)一词的取用，已能无遗地含摄入息等身，然因其由众多微聚(kalāpa)的集合而成，为显示其所有部分皆能被感受，故取用“各”(paṭi)一词。于此，为显示其审慎行持的状态，故取用“善”(saṃ)一词。为阐明此义，故说“于全部……”(sakalassā’ti)等。于此，正如在(修习)入出息时，虽然修行者(yogi)的修行方法是相同的，但为了开示应于每一(入息、出息)都审慎地修行，故(世尊)作了分别的教示。同样地，为阐明此义，虽然意义相同，亦应了知，(注疏者)以“于全部……”等，对(此)二句作了分别的释义。“令其显现”(Pākaṭaṃ karonto)，即令其清晰，意为使其全面明了。“显现化”(pākaṭīkaraṇa)即是“明了”(vibhāvanaṃ)，于此不迷乱，是唯以智使其(入出息)生起。为开示此义，故说“如是令其了知……”(evaṃ viditaṃ karonto’ti)等。于此，关于“是故”(tasmā)的文义结合(yojanā)应知：因为(yasmā)是以与智相应之心使入出息生起，而非以不相应之心，是故(tasmā)，佛陀等说，如此之人被称为修学“我将觉知全身而入息，……而出息”者。“粉碎散布”(Cuṇṇavicuṇṇavisaṭe)，即因其具有众多微聚，而以粉碎的状态散布。(入出息的)开端之所以显现，是凭借念与智之力，以及先前之行(pubbābhisaṅkhāra)的发动。“当成为如是者”，即当成为如第四种人(puggala)那样的人。其意涵是：应预先安立念与智，于(入出息的)三处都只使与智相应之心生起。
entries.english: 220. ‘Experiencing the whole body’ means: one who is by nature properly and individually experiencing and knowing the entire body; or, for whom there is a proper and individual experience of it; or, one who is properly and individually experiencing it. This is the meaning. Therein, although the complete inclusion of the body of breath, etc., is established by the taking of the word ‘whole,’ the word ‘paṭi’ (each, individually) is used to show the experiencing of all its parts, because it is an aggregate of many groups of material qualities. Therein, the word ‘saṃ’ (well, thoroughly) is used to show the state of being one who acts carefully. Showing this meaning, the text states ‘of the entire body,’ etc. Therein, just as, although the method of practice for the yogī regarding the in-breaths and out-breaths is the same, a separate teaching was given to show that one should practice each one carefully, so too, to illuminate that very meaning, it should be known that although there is a similarity of meaning, a separate explanation of the meaning for the two phrases was made. ‘Making it clear’ means making it evident, thoroughly clarifying it. This making clear, this clarification, which is non-bewilderment regarding them, happens by directing them with knowledge alone, as stated in the text beginning ‘thus making it known.’ Therein, ‘therefore’ means: since one produces the in-breaths and out-breaths only with a mind associated with knowledge, not with a mind dissociated from it, therefore such a person is said by the Buddhas and others to be one who trains thus: ‘I will breathe in, I will breathe out, experiencing the whole body.’ This is the connection. ‘Scattered as if ground to powder’ refers to being scattered in a state of being ground to powder due to being a multitude of many groups of material qualities. The beginning becomes manifest by means of mindfulness and knowledge, and because of the operation of previous formations in that way. ‘One must become like that’ means one must become like the fourth type of person; having established mindfulness and knowledge from the very beginning, one should produce a mind associated with knowledge in all three instances. This is the intention.

entries.pali: Rasaggasaggī ti ettha rasaṃ gasanti harantīti rasaggasā. Rasaharaṇīnametaṃ adhivacanaṃ, tā aggā assāti rasaggasaggī. Mahāpurisassa kira sattarasaharaṇīsahassāni uddhaggāni hutvā gīvāyameva paṭimukkāni. Tilaphalamattopi āhāro jivhagge ṭhapito sabbakāyaṃ anupharati. Teneva mahāpadhānaṃ padahantassa ekataṇḍulādīhipi kaḷāyayūsapasatamattenāpi kāyassa yāpanaṃ ahosi. Aññesaṃ pana tathā abhāvā na sakalaṃ kāyaṃ ojā pharati. Tena te bahvābādhā honti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 具最上味觉者(Rasaggasaggī)。于此，能传导滋味者，称为“味传导脉”(rasaggasā)，此为味传导脉之异名。因其具有最上的彼等脉管，故称“具最上味觉者”。据说大士有七千条味传导脉，其末端向上，皆汇于颈项。因此，纵使仅有芝麻大小的食物置于舌尖，其滋养亦能遍满全身。正因如此，当他行大精进时，即便只食一粒米，或饮一掬豆汁，亦足以维持身体。而他人则无此能力，故营养精华无法遍及全身，是以多诸疾病。
entries.english: Regarding “possessing the supreme taste” (rasaggasaggī): herein, rasaggasā means 'they convey taste' (rasaṃ gasanti). This is a term for the taste-conveying nerves. Because those nerves are supreme (aggā) in him, he is called rasaggasaggī. It is said that the Great Being has seven thousand taste-conveying nerves that, with their tips pointing upwards, are connected within his neck. Even a morsel of food the size of a sesame seed, when placed on the tip of his tongue, pervades his entire body. For this reason, while he was undertaking the Great Striving, the sustenance of his body was possible even with single grains of rice and so on, or with just a handful of bean soup. For others, however, because this is not the case, the nutritive essence does not pervade the entire body. Therefore, they suffer from many illnesses.

entries.pali: Paccayā cīvarādayo garukātabbā etesanti paccayagarukā, āmisacakkhukāti attho. Paccayesu giddhā gadhitā paccayānaṃ bahulabhāvāya paṭipannāti paccayabāhulikā . Bhagavatopi pākaṭā ahosi pakaticārittavasenāti adhippāyo aññathā apākaṭasseva abhāvato. Dhammasabhāvacintāvasena pavattaṃ sahottappañāṇaṃ dhammasaṃvego, idha pana so bhikkhūnaṃ lābhagarutādhammavasena veditabbo. Samaṇadhammavuttī ti samaṇadhammakaraṇaṃ. Sā ti dhammadāyādadesanā. Paṭibimbadassanavasena sabbakāyassa dassanayoggo ādāsoti sabbakāyikaādāso .
entries.chinese_simplified: 于衣等资具心怀敬重，故称‘重资具者’，意即眼见物质。于资具贪婪、执著，为求资具丰足而行，故称‘多求资具者’。此行亦因其本然之行仪而显明于世尊，此是意趣；否则，无有不显明者。因思惟诸法自性而生起具惭愧之智，是为‘法悚惧’；于此，当知是比丘因重利养之法而有。‘沙门法行’即行沙门法。‘彼’指《法嗣经》之教示。能映现全身之镜，故称‘全身镜’。
entries.english: ‘Those who regard requisites as important’ (paccayagarukā) means that requisites such as robes should be regarded as important by them; the meaning is ‘those whose eye is on material things’ (āmisacakkhukā). ‘Those who pursue an abundance of requisites’ (paccayabāhulikā) means those who are greedy for requisites, attached to them, and committed to the increase of requisites. The meaning is that the Blessed One, too, became renowned through his natural conduct; otherwise, there would be no one who is not renowned. The knowledge accompanied by moral dread that arises through reflection on the nature of phenomena is ‘spiritual urgency’ (dhammasaṃvego); here, however, it should be understood in the sense of the bhikkhus' high regard for gains. ‘Living by the ascetic’s duty’ (samaṇadhammavuttī) means the performance of ascetic duties. ‘That’ (sā) refers to the teaching on inheriting the Dhamma. ‘A mirror for the whole body’ (sabbakāyikaādāso) means a mirror suitable for seeing the entire body by way of reflection.

entries.pali: Sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī ti sabbassa kāyassa paṭi paṭi paccekaṃ sammadeva vedanasīlo jānanasīlo, tassa vā paṭi paṭi sammadeva vedo etassa atthi, taṃ vā paṭi paṭi sammadeva vedamānoti attho. Tattha tattha sabba-ggahaṇena assāsādikāyassa anavasesapariyādāne siddhepi anekakalāpasamudāyabhāvato tassa sabbesampi bhāgānaṃ saṃvedanadassanatthaṃ paṭi-saddaggahaṇaṃ, tattha sakkaccakāribhāvadassanatthaṃ saṃ-saddaggahaṇanti imamatthaṃ dassento ‘‘sakalassā’’ tiādimāha. Tattha yathā samānesupi assāsapassāsesu yogino paṭipattividhāne paccekaṃ sakkaccaṃyeva paṭipajjitabbanti dassetuṃ visuṃ desanā katā, evaṃ tamevatthaṃ dīpetuṃ satipi atthassa samānatāya ‘‘sakalassā’’tiādinā padadvayassa visuṃ visuṃ atthavaṇṇanā katāti veditabbā. Pākaṭaṃ karonto ti vibhūtaṃ karonto, sabbaso vibhāventoti attho. Pākaṭīkaraṇaṃ vibhāvanaṃ tattha asammuyhanañāṇeneva nesaṃ pavattanena hotīti dassento ‘‘evaṃ viditaṃ karonto’’ tiādimāha . Tattha tasmā ti yasmā ñāṇasampayuttacitteneva assāsapassāse pavatteti, na vippayuttacittena, tasmā evaṃbhūto sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmi passasissāmīti sikkhatīti vuccati buddhādīhīti yojanā. Cuṇṇavicuṇṇavisaṭe ti anekakalāpatāya cuṇṇavicuṇṇabhāvena visaṭe. Ādi pākaṭo hoti satiyā ñāṇassa ca vasena katapubbābhisaṅkhārassa pavattattā. Tādisena bhavitabba nti catutthapuggalasadisena bhavitabbaṃ, pageva satiṃ ñāṇañca paccupaṭṭhapetvā tīsupi ṭhānesu ñāṇasampayuttameva cittaṃ pavattetabbanti adhippāyo.
entries.chinese_simplified: “感受全身者”(Sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī)：意指对全身的每一部分都正确地有感受、有认知；或他具有对每一部分的正确感受；或他正在正确地感受每一部分。于此，虽然用“全”(sabba)一词已能成就对入出息身的无遗摄取，但由于（入出息身）是众多色聚(kalāpa)的集合，为了显示对所有部分的感受，而取“遍”(paṭi)一词；为了显示恭敬而行的状态，而取“善”(saṃ)一词。为了显示此义，而说“对全体”(sakalassa)等。于此，如同在同样的入出息中，为了显示禅修者应于每一部分都恭敬地修行，而作了分别的教示；同样地，为了阐明此义，虽然意义相同，但仍对“对全体”(sakalassa)等两个词作了分别的释义，当知。“令其显现”(Pākaṭaṃ karonto)：即令其清晰，意为完全地辨明。令其显现、辨明是通过不迷乱之智的运作而发生的，为显示此，而说“如是了知”(evaṃ viditaṃ karonto)等。于此，“因此”(tasmā)：因为只以与智相应的心令入出息运作，不以不相应的心，因此，这样的人被称为‘我将感受全身而入息，我将感受全身而出息地学习’，此乃佛陀等所说，应如是结合。“于粉碎散布”(Cuṇṇavicuṇṇavisaṭe)：即由于是众多色聚，而呈粉碎散布之态。由于念与智的力量，先前所造作的（呼吸）过程发生，其开端变得明显。“应成为如此”(Tādisena bhavitabbaṃ)：即应成为像第四种人那样。其要义是，首先就要建立起念与智，在（呼吸的）所有三处都只让与智相应的心运作。
entries.english: ‘Experiencing the whole body’: one who has the habit of feeling or knowing each and every part of the entire body quite well; or, for that person, there is the feeling of each and every part quite well; or, one who experiences it quite well—this is the meaning. There, although by the taking of ‘whole,’ the complete inclusion of the body of in-breaths, etc., is accomplished, because it is a collection of many aggregates, the prefix ‘paṭi-’ is taken to show the experiencing of all its parts. There, the prefix ‘saṃ-’ is taken to show the state of acting with care. Showing this meaning, he said ‘of the entire,’ etc. There, just as a separate teaching was given to show that in the method of practice, the meditator should practice each part with care even when the in-breaths and out-breaths are similar, so too, to illuminate that very meaning, it should be known that a separate explanation of the meaning of the two phrases beginning with ‘of the entire’ has been made, even though their meaning is similar. ‘Making it clear’: making it evident, making it fully manifest—this is the meaning. Making clear is clarification. Therein, it happens through their proceeding only with non-bewildered knowledge. Showing this, he said ‘knowing it thus,’ etc. There, ‘therefore’: because one causes the in-breaths and out-breaths to proceed only with a mind associated with knowledge, not with a mind dissociated from it, therefore such a one who trains thus, ‘I will breathe in experiencing the whole body, I will breathe out experiencing the whole body,’ is called so by the Buddhas and others—this is the connection. ‘Scattered like fine powder’: scattered in the manner of fine powder due to being a collection of many kalāpas. In the beginning, it becomes clear by the power of mindfulness and knowledge, due to the proceeding of the previously made formation. ‘One should become like that’: one should become like the fourth person. Having first established mindfulness and knowledge, one should cause the mind associated with knowledge to proceed in all three places—this is the intention.

entries.pali: Eva nti vuttappakārena sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedanavaseneva. Ghaṭatī ti ussahati. Vāyamatī ti vāyāmaṃ karoti, manasikāraṃ pavattetīti attho. Tathābhūtassā ti ānāpānassatiṃ bhāventassa. Saṃvaro ti sati vīriyampi vā. Tāya satiyā ti yā sā ānāpāne ārabbha pavattā sati, tāya. Tena manasikārenā ti yo so tattha satipubbaṅgamo bhāvanāmanasikāro, tena saddhinti adhippāyo. Āsevatī ti ‘‘tisso sikkhāyo’’ti vutte adhikusaladhamme āsevati. Tadāsevanañhettha sikkhananti adhippetaṃ. Purimanaye ti purimasmiṃ bhāvanānaye, paṭhamavatthudvayeti adhippāyo. Tatthāpi kāmaṃ ñāṇuppādanaṃ labbhateva assāsapassāsānaṃ yāthāvato dīgharassabhāvāvabodhasabbhāvato, tathāpi taṃ na dukkaraṃ yathāpavattānaṃ tesaṃ gahaṇamattabhāvatoti tattha vattamānakālappayogo kato. Idaṃ pana dukkaraṃ purisassa khuradhārāyaṃ gamanasadisaṃ, tasmā sātisayenettha pubbābhisaṅkhārena bhavitabbanti dīpetuṃ anāgatakālappayogo katoti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘tattha yasmā’’ tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ñāṇuppādanādīsū ti ādi -saddena kāyasaṅkhārapassambhanapītipaṭisaṃvedanādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Keci panettha ‘‘saṃvarasamādānānaṃ saṅgaho’’ti vadanti.
entries.chinese_simplified: “如是”是指通过上述方式，即通过感受全身。“他努力”即他奋力。“他勤奋”即他付出努力，意思是发起作意。“对于那样的人”是指对于修习入出息念的人。“防护”是指念，或也是指精进。“通过那念”是指通过那缘于入出息而生起的念。“通过那作意”是指通过那以念为前导的修习作意，其意趣是“与……一起”。“他修习”是指他修习在“三学(tisso sikkhāyo)”中所说的增上善法，于此，那修习意指学习。“在前述方法中”是指在前面的修习方法中，意指在最初的两个事中。在那里，虽然由于确实存在着对入出息长短状态的如实了知，所以能获得智的生起，但那并不困难，因为只是把握如其所起的它们，因此那里使用了现在时态。但这事是困难的，如同一个人在剃刀边缘行走，因此为了阐明于此必须有卓越的先前行，而使用了将来时态。为了显示此义，而说了“于彼，因为”等。在“智的生起等”中，通过“等”字包含了身行(kāyasaṅkhāra)的平息、喜的感受等。于此，有些人说：“这是防护与受持的集合。”
entries.english: ‘Thus’: in the manner explained, it is precisely by way of experiencing the whole body. ‘Strives’ means makes an effort. ‘Exerts’ means puts forth energy, the meaning being that one directs attention. ‘For one such as this’ refers to one who develops mindfulness of breathing. ‘Restraint’ refers to mindfulness or energy. ‘By that mindfulness’ means by that mindfulness which has arisen concerning the in-and-out breaths. ‘By that attention’ refers to that attention in development which is preceded by mindfulness; the intention is ‘together with that’. ‘Practices’ means one cultivates higher wholesome qualities, as stated in ‘the three trainings’. Here, it is intended that the practice of those qualities is the training. ‘In the previous way’ refers to the earlier method of development; the intention is in the first two subjects. There, indeed, the arising of knowledge can be achieved regarding the true nature of the in-and-out breaths—whether long or short—because of the possibility of discerning them correctly. Yet, it is not difficult because it is merely the grasping of their occurrence as they arise. Thus, the present tense is used there. But this is difficult, like a person walking on a razor’s edge. Therefore, to show that extraordinary preliminary effort must be made here, the future tense is used. To explain this meaning, it is said, ‘because therein,’ etc. ‘Therein, in the arising of knowledge, etc.’—the word ‘etc.’ includes the calming of bodily formations, the experiencing of joy, and so on. Some, however, say here that it refers to the inclusion of restraint and undertaking.

entries.work_title: 阿毗达摩入门-名色分别 Abhidhammāvatāro-Nāmarūpaparicchedo
entries.pali: Ādimajjhāvasānaṃ tu, karonto viditaṃ tathā; Samāhito sabbakāya-paṭisaṃvedi sikkhati.
entries.chinese_simplified: 他训练自己：了知（呼吸）之初、中、后，觉知全身，心入于定。
entries.english: Making known the beginning, middle, and end, thus composed, one trains experiencing the entire body.

entries.pali: 66 . Paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ natthi sevetukāmatā maggena maggappaṭipattīti dvinnaṃ aṅgānaṃ siddhattā. Dūsitassa pana maggena maggappaṭipatti evamekaṃ aṅgaṃ siddhaṃ, sevetukāmatāsaṅkhātaṃ sādiyanaṃ asiddhaṃ. Tasmā so pucchitvā ‘‘sādiyi’’nti vuttapaṭiññāya nāsetabbo. Tatthevā ti vesāliyaṃ mahāvane eva. Sabbaṅgagata nti sabbakāyagataṃ. ‘‘Lohitaṃ viyā’’ti vuttattā kesādīnaṃ vinimuttaṭṭhāne sabbatthāti gahetabbaṃ. Niccameva ummattako hotī ti yassa pittakosato pittaṃ calitvā sabbadā bahi nikkhantaṃ hoti, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yassa pana pittaṃ calitvā pittakoseyeva ṭhitaṃ hoti, kadāci vā nikkhantaṃ puna nikkhamati, sopi antarantarā saññaṃ paṭilabhati bhesajjena ca pakatiārogyaṃ paṭilabhatīti veditabbaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 66. 因‘欲求交往’及‘道入于道’二支已成就，故无需令其承认。但对已遭毁坏者而言，‘道入于道’此一支已成就，而名为‘欲求交往’的‘乐受’尚未成就。是故应询问彼，以其所说‘我已乐受’之承诺而驱摈之。‘就在彼处’(tattheva)，即就在毗舍离(Vesālī)的大林中。‘遍身’(Sabbaṅgagataṃ)即遍及全身。因说‘如血’，故应理解为于发等脱离之处，遍及一切。‘恒为癫狂者’，是指其胆汁从胆囊中动移而恒常流出者，就此而说。但若其胆汁动移后仍住于胆囊，或有时流出而复流出，彼亦能时而复得其想，并能以药复得平常健康，应如是知。
entries.english: 66. There is no making of a confession, because of the accomplishment of two factors: the desire to engage and the penetration of the path by the path. But for one who has been violated, one factor, the penetration of the path by the path, is accomplished; however, the consent, known as 'the desire to engage,' is not accomplished. Therefore, he should be questioned, and when he confesses by saying, 'I consented,' he is to be expelled. 'There' means right in the Great Forest at Vesālī. 'Pervading all limbs' means pervading the whole body. Since it is said 'like blood,' it should be understood as being everywhere in places free from hair and so on. 'One who is always insane': this is said referring to one whose bile, having been agitated from the gallbladder, is always flowing out. But it should be understood that one whose bile, having been agitated, remains right in the gallbladder, or which, having sometimes flowed out, flows out again—he too intermittently regains perception and, through medicine, recovers his normal health.

entries.pali: Ittaravasenā ti parittakālavasena. Tādiso ti dīgho rasso ca. Vaṇṇā ti dīghādiākārā. Nāsikaggeva bhikkhuno ti nāsikagge vā, vā -saddena uttaroṭṭhe vāti attho. Tasmā ti yasmā ‘‘ādimajjhapariyosānavasena sabbaṃ assāsapassāsakāyaṃ viditaṃ pākaṭaṃ karissāmī’’ti pubbe pavattaābhogavasena pacchā tathā samuppannena ñāṇasampayuttacittena taṃ assāsapassāsakāyaṃ evaṃ viditaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto assasati ceva passasati ca, tasmā evaṃbhūto sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmi passasissāmīti sikkhati nāma, na pana ‘‘anāgate evaṃ karissāmī’’ti cintanamattena so evaṃ vuccatīti adhippāyo. Tathābhūtassā ti ādimajjhapariyosānaṃ viditaṃ karontassa. Saṃvaro ti sati vīriyampi vā. Na aññaṃ kiñcī ti sabbakāyaṃ viditaṃ karissāmītiādikaṃ pubbābhogaṃ sandhāya vadati. Ñāṇuppādanādīsū ti ādi -saddena kāyasaṅkhārapassambhanapītipaṭisaṃvedanādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kāyasaṅkhāra nti assāsapassāsaṃ. So hi cittasamuṭṭhānopi samāno karajakāyapaṭibaddhavuttitāya tena saṅkharīyatīti kāyasaṅkhāroti vuccati. Apariggahitakāle ti kammaṭṭhānassa anāraddhakāle, tadārambhatthāya kāyacittānampi apariggahitakāleti attho. Nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāyāti hi iminā kāyapariggaho, parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvāti iminā cittapariggaho vutto. Adhimatta nti balavaṃ oḷārikaṃ, liṅgavipallāsena vuttaṃ. Kāyasaṅkhāro hi adhippeto. Adhimattaṃ hutvā pavattatīti kiriyāvisesanaṃ vā etaṃ. Sabbesaṃyevā ti ubhayesampi.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘短暂地’，是指时间短促地。‘如是’，是指长与短。‘色’，是指长等形状。‘比丘于鼻尖’，是指于鼻尖，或通过‘或’字，其义为于上唇。‘所以’，是说：由于先前以‘我将令整个入出息身，从初、中、后皆被了知、显现’而作意，其后以如是生起的与智相应之心，如此了知、显现彼入出息身而入息、出息；所以，这样的人才名为修学‘我将觉知全身而入息，我将觉知全身而出息’。并非仅以‘我未来将如此做’的思量，便可被称为如此，此为意趣。‘如是之人’，是指令初、中、后显了者。‘防护’，是指念，或亦是精进。‘非任何其他’，是指针对‘我将了知全身’等先前之作意而言。‘于智生起等中’，‘等’字包含身行止息、觉受喜等。‘身行’，是指入出息。彼虽由心生，然因其作用与业生身相连，由彼所造作，故称为身行。‘未把握时’，是指未开始修习业处时，为开始修习，身心亦未把握之时，此为义。以‘结跏趺坐，端正身体’说为把握身，以‘置念于面前’说为把握心。‘极’，是指强力、粗显，此是以语性转换而说。此中意指身行。或此为‘成为极强而转起’的动词状语。‘一切’，是指两者皆是。
entries.english: By 'for a short time' (ittaravasena) is meant by way of a brief period. 'Such' (tādiso) means both long and short. 'Appearance' (vaṇṇā) means forms such as long, etc. 'For a bhikkhu at the tip of the nose' (nāsikaggeva bhikkhuno) means either at the tip of the nose or, by the word 'or' (vā), at the upper lip; this is the meaning. 'Therefore' (tasmā): because, by means of a previously arisen reflection, 'I will make the entire body of in-breaths and out-breaths known and manifest by way of its beginning, middle, and end,' and afterwards with a mind associated with knowledge that has arisen in such a way, one makes that body of in-breaths and out-breaths thus known and manifest while breathing in and breathing out, therefore, being such, one trains, 'Experiencing the whole body, I will breathe in; I will breathe out.' The intention is that one is not called so merely by thinking, 'I will do so in the future.' 'Of one who is such' (tathābhūtassa) means of one who makes the beginning, middle, and end known. 'Restraint' (saṃvaro) means mindfulness or also energy. 'Not anything else' (na aññaṃ kiñci): this is said with reference to the preliminary reflection, 'I will make the whole body known,' etc. 'In the arising of knowledge, etc.' (ñāṇuppādanādīsu): by the word 'etc.' (ādi), it includes the calming of the bodily formation, the experiencing of rapture, etc. 'The bodily formation' (kāyasaṅkhāraṃ) means the in-and-out-breaths. For although it is mind-born, because its occurrence is connected with the physical body, it is conditioned by that and is thus called 'bodily formation.' 'At a time when it has not been grasped' (apariggahitakāle) means at a time when the meditation subject has not been undertaken; the meaning is the time when, for the purpose of undertaking it, the body and mind have not yet been grasped. For by 'He sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect' the grasping of the body is stated; by 'and established mindfulness in front of him' the grasping of the mind is stated. 'Excessive' (adhimattaṃ) means strong, gross; it is stated with a change of gender, for the bodily formation is intended. Or this is an adverbial qualifier of the action: 'occurring excessively' (adhimattaṃ hutvā pavattati). 'Of all' (sabbesaṃyeva) means of both teachers.
